quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: When parking uphill on a road with no curb, set the parking brake and turn your wheels:

options.text: Toward the edge of the road.
Away from the edge of the road.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This helps the vehicle roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle and see the road ahead.
Because other drivers pull behind large vehicles before passing.
Because you can get caught in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle and see the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Large truck and bus drivers cannot see vehicles directly behind them. Increase your distance to see around the vehicle and watch the road ahead.

questions.question: When roads are slippery after rain starts, you should:

options.text: Avoid making fast turns and stops.
Test your tires' grip while going uphill.
Look closer to your vehicle instead of ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire traction. Drive slowly and avoid sharp turns or sudden stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: What must you do on a green arrow?

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield only to pedestrians in the intersection.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. First, yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection, then turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign ahead.
Side road entering from the left.
Stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells you a yield sign is coming. Start slowing down when you see it.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline while in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline while in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your blind spot and watch for other drivers in the same lane. Never try to pass or change lanes inside an intersection.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid out of control, you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes lightly.
Stay off the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, do not use the brakes. Keep steering until the car is under control and moving safely.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, you should:

options.text: Have one rear wheel touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
Keep your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and put the car in park when parked on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your wheels away from traffic. If there is a curb, turn wheels toward it when going uphill or away from it when going downhill.

questions.question: Large trucks often lose speed when:

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.
Driving through long, gradual curves.
Driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more time to speed up than cars. They lose speed going uphill. Give trucks extra space, especially on hills.

questions.question: When you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the other driver will drive at the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way, even when you use your turn signal.

questions.question: When should you start slowing down before exiting the interstate?

options.text: About halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed steady until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to the speed posted for the exit ramp.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow light at an intersection and have not entered it yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass the light before it turns red.
Slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means stop if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, keep going at a safe speed.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then cross when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down to a safe speed and proceed with caution.

questions.question: How can you avoid glare from oncoming headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Look at the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Do not look at bright oncoming lights. Instead, glance toward the right side of the road. Then look ahead to watch where the other vehicle is.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on the road or shoulder. Drive to the next exit instead. Other drivers will not expect you to back up, and this could cause a crash.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, what speed should you drive?

options.text: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
5 to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
The posted speed limit for the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the same speed as the other traffic.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines mean on streets and highways?

options.text: No passing is allowed.
They separate lanes moving in the same direction.
They separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: They separate lanes moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic going opposite ways. Dashed lines mean you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: No turns are allowed.
The road narrows ahead.
There are curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns about a winding road.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire blows out while driving?

options.text: Press and hold the brake.
Hold the wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by easing off the gas and braking lightly. Pull off the road to a safe spot if possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge right.
Divided highway begins.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane is ending ahead. Drivers in that lane need to merge into another lane.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left to get ready to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Always signal about 100 feet before you turn. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: You and another driver reach a four-way stop at the same time. The other driver is on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to turn has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two cars reach a four-way stop at the same time, the car on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: When you are following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, add extra space in front of your car. Slow down gradually or change lanes. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass another car on the left if there is no oncoming traffic. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing red light at an intersection?

options.text: Stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, then go when safe.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Stop completely and wait until the light stops flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, make sure it is safe, then proceed.
